{{Short description|Mathematical function}}
{{distinguish|text=[[confluent hypergeometric function|Kummer's confluent hypergeometric function]]}}

In [[mathematics]], '''Kummer's function''', named after [[Ernst Kummer]], is a [[complex analysis|complex function]] related to the [[polylogarithm]]. It is defined by{{sfnp|Lewin|1991|loc=chapter 3}}

:<math>\Lambda_n(z)=\int_0^z \frac{\log^{n-1}|t|}{1+t}\;dt.</math>

Its [[duplication formula]] is

:<math>\Lambda_n(z)+\Lambda_n(-z)= 2^{1-n}\Lambda_n(-z^2)</math>.

Compare this to the duplication formula for the polylogarithm:

:<math>\operatorname{Li}_n(z)+\operatorname{Li}_n(-z)= 2^{1-n}\operatorname{Li}_n(z^2).</math>

An explicit link to the polylogarithm is given by

:<math>\operatorname{Li}_n(z)=\operatorname{Li}_n(1)\;\;+\;\;
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (-1)^{k-1} \;\frac{\log^k |z|} {k!} \;\operatorname{Li}_{n-k} (z) \;\;+\;\;
\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{(n-1)!} \;\left[ \Lambda_n(-1) - \Lambda_n(-z) \right].</math>
